title: Speed-tiered concurrent scorer with adaptive token budgets and hard timeboxes
creator: Aisha Fernandez
description: Reduce p95/p99 latency for the reranking endpoint while preserving quality and throughput. Implement a speed-tiered concurrency scheme that assigns candidate partitions to fast vs best-effort lanes, enforce per-request token budgets, and add hard timeboxes to prevent tail amplification from long-context scorers. This ticket covers design, prototype, canary rollout, and measurement plan.
background: Current reranker suffers from occasional long tail latency when single requests contain very long candidate sequences or models use long KV cache paths. Existing microbatching groups requests but can be dominated by outliers. We need a solution that parallelizes scoring across lane priorities, caps per-request token usage, and ensures bounded service time under load without significant QA regressions in ranking quality.
design_decisions: Introduce two execution lanes: 'fast' (low-latency, small token budgets, stricter CPU/GPU quotas) and 'throughput' (higher token budgets, batched, best-effort hedging).
Partition candidate sets into shards sized by token_estimate so each shard fits within token budget targets. Use deterministic sharding to preserve reproducibility.
Enforce per-request token_budget computed from request metadata (max_tokens_per_candidate * num_candidates) capped by tenant tier and global ceiling.

Apply hard timebox per lane (e.g., fast lane 120ms, throughput lane 600ms) with a soft-hedge: if timebox expires, return partial scores and mark candidate remainder for background scoring or fallback.
Non-blocking KV prefetch: fetch KV cache asynchronously before tokenized scoring step and expose prefetch success/failure metrics for routing decisions.
Backpressure: when queue depth for fast lane exceeds threshold, probabilistically demote requests to throughput lane to protect tail SLOs.
Instrumentation: expose per-request token_consumed, lane_assigned, shard_count, timebox_expired, and partial_result flags to Console for rollouts.
Quality guardrails: instrument pairwise A/B ranking comparator against baseline on canary traffic; require <0.5% decrease in NDCG@10 before broader rollout.
implementation_plan: Week 1: Prototype sharding + token_budget enforcement in a feature branch. Add unit tests for budget enforcement and deterministic sharder.
Week 2: Implement async KV prefetch and lane router with simple heuristics (candidate tokens, request priority header). Add metrics and traces.
Week 3: Integrate per-lane timeboxes and partial-result gating. Add fallback path for background scoring or simplified model variant.
Week 4: Run internal perf tests (k8s dev cluster) with synthetic workloads (short/long candidate mixes) and collect p50/p95/p99, GPU utilization, and token cost per request.
Week 5: Canary rollout (10%) with A/B comparator on production traffic and daily quality dashboard. If metrics stable, incrementally ramp to 50% then 100%.
Post-release: Add autoscaler hints so Dedicated pools can pre-provision fast-lane capacity for high-commit customers.
Deliverables: design doc, PRs for runtime + router + console metrics, perf dashboard, runbook for incidents.
acceptance_criteria: p95 latency for rerank endpoint decreases by >= 15% on typical query mix in staging compared to current baseline.
p99 latency does not regress more than 5% and tail failures due to timeouts are <0.1% of requests after canary.
NDCG@10 measured on held-out rerank testset degrades by <0.5% versus baseline and is monitored continuously.
All new metrics (lane_assigned, token_consumed, timebox_expired) are visible in Console and used to drive canary alerts.
Canary rollout plan executed with automated rollback if CPU/GPU or error budget thresholds breached.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Demotion to throughput lane could increase latency for some premium customers. Mitigation: respect tenant-tier pinning to prevent demotion for reserved Dedicated capacity.

Risk: Partial scoring may reduce relevance. Mitigation: run pairwise ranking comparisons and keep partial-score fallback only when quality impact is small; queue remainder for best-effort background scoring.
Risk: KV prefetch failures may increase token cost for cold paths. Mitigation: fall back to synchronous fetch in rare failure cases and track error rate; tune prefetch concurrency.
Risk: More complex routing increases operator burden. Mitigation: ship clear Console dashboards and a compact runbook with recommended knobs and thresholds.
progress_updates: 2025-02-20: Spike complete. PoC shows deterministic sharder reduces single-request long-run scoring time by ~30% in synthetic test.
2025-02-26: Async KV prefetch implemented and instrumented; observed 12% improvement in median scorer step latency in dev cluster.
2025-03-03: Timebox enforcement and partial-result path landed in PR #8421. Running integration smoke tests; discovered edge case with zero-candidate requests which is being handled in fallback.
2025-03-05: Began canary plan drafting and updated Console charts for lane metrics. Preparing load tests for next week to validate p99 under 2x traffic.
qa_notes: Create synthetic replay with mixed candidate lengths (short/medium/very-long) and validate lane assignment distribution.
Run deterministic seeding for sharder tests to ensure no flakiness in acceptance suites.
Add regression test that ensures token_budget cap cannot be bypassed via malformed requests.
Verify monitoring alerts trigger when timebox_expired rate > 0.2% during canary.
rollback_plan: If canary shows p99 regressions >5% or NDCG drops >0.5% or error rate spikes, revert router flag to previous stable and scale fast-lane capacity down; notify SRE and open an incident with tag rerank-timebox-rollback.
